intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the maze-like streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from legendary local vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Join a guided walking food tour or explore independently using a street food map.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival & Night Market
experiences.description: Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An, visit centuries-old merchant houses, tailors, and temples, then experience the magical monthly Lantern Festival where the town glows with hundreds of silk lanterns. Sample Cao Lau and White Rose dumplings from local market stalls unique to this region.

experiences.name: Motorbike Loop Through Ha Giang
experiences.description: Rent a semi-automatic motorbike and tackle the legendary Ha Giang Loop, a backpacker favorite winding through dramatic karst mountains, rice terraces, and remote ethnic minority villages including Hmong and Tay communities. Stop at Dong Van Karst Plateau Geopark and Ma Pi Leng Pass for breathtaking views.

experiences.name: Mekong Delta Sampan Boat & Local Market Experience
experiences.description: Board a traditional wooden sampan boat through narrow canals of the Mekong Delta, visiting the famous Cai Rang Floating Market at dawn where vendors sell tropical fruits and local produce directly from boats. Stop at riverside workshops producing rice paper, coconut candy, and honey, then enjoy a home-cooked lunch with a local family.

experiences.name: Hue Imperial Citadel & Royal Cuisine Tasting
experiences.description: Explore the grand Imperial Citadel and royal tombs of the Nguyen Dynasty in the former Vietnamese capital of Hue. Afterward, dive into Hue's distinctive royal cuisine — considered Vietnam's most refined — by sampling Banh Khoai crispy pancakes, Bun Bo Hue spicy noodle soup, and Com Hen clam rice from street stalls along the Perfume River.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hanoi airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take a budget airport bus (Bus 86, ~45,000 VND) or negotiate a metered taxi to Old Quarter. Check in to Boutique Stay in Old Quarter.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely orientation walk through the Old Quarter's 36 ancient streets. Explore Hang Gai (Silk Street), Hang Bac (Silver Street), and the surrounding alleyways. Visit Hoan Kiem Lake and snap photos of Ngoc Son Temple from the iconic red Huc Bridge (entry ~30,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the famous Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street (open Fri–Sun, but surrounding streets are always lively). Stroll Ta Hien Street — known as 'Beer Corner' — for cheap bia hoi (fresh draught beer, ~5,000–10,000 VND per glass) and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Grab something light at the hotel or skip — you arrive at 13:00.
meals.lunch: Bun Cha Huong Lien (famous spot near Old Quarter) — bun cha (grilled pork with noodles) for ~60,000–80,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Banh Mi 25 on Hang Ca Street — legendary bánh mì sandwiches for ~35,000–50,000 VND each. Eat at a plastic stool on the street.

day_by_day.notes: Get VND cash from an ATM at the airport (Vietcombank has low fees). Buy a local SIM card (Viettel or Vietnamobile, ~100,000 VND with data). Keep your bag close in the Old Quarter — it's safe but busy.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (6:00–7:00 AM) for the authentic Old Quarter morning experience. Join locals at a street-side pho stall for breakfast. Then visit Hoa Lo Prison Museum ('Hanoi Hilton') — entry ~30,000 VND — for a powerful look at Vietnamese and American War history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) — entry ~30,000 VND — Vietnam's first university dating to 1070. Explore the beautifully preserved courtyards and learn about Confucian education. Afterward, walk to the nearby Fine Arts Museum (~40,000 VND) to see traditional lacquerware, sculpture, and folk art.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter for the Friday Night Market on Hang Dao. Browse handicrafts, clothing, and street food stalls. Watch a free outdoor performance or live music near Hoan Kiem Lake.

meals.breakfast: Street-side pho bo (beef pho) near the hotel — ~40,000–60,000 VND per bowl.
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Nam Bo on Hang Dieu Street — dry beef noodle salad for ~60,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Night market street food crawl — try nem ran (fried spring rolls), banh trang nuong (grilled rice paper), and che (sweet dessert soup) for ~80,000–120,000 VND total.

day_by_day.notes: Temple of Literature closes at 5:30 PM. Wear modest clothing (covered shoulders and knees) as a sign of respect. April weather in Hanoi may be warm and slightly humid — carry a small water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex (free entry, open ~8:00–11:00 AM, closed Mon/Fri). See the One Pillar Pagoda and Ho Chi Minh Museum (~40,000 VND). The Ba Dinh Square area is peaceful and historically rich in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND) — one of Southeast Asia's best ethnographic museums showcasing 54 ethnic minority groups. Spend 2–3 hours exploring indoor and outdoor exhibits including full-scale traditional houses. Take a local bus back (~7,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Book a traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Theatre (~100,000 VND for budget seats) — a uniquely Vietnamese art form. Afterward, explore the atmospheric streets around St. Joseph's Cathedral at night.

meals.breakfast: Banh cuon (steamed rice rolls with pork and mushroom) from a street vendor near the hotel — ~40,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Bun Cha Obama (same shop visited by Obama) on Le Van Huu Street — ~80,000 VND for the full set.
meals.dinner: Pho Thin on Dinh Tien Hoang — legendary Hanoi pho for ~60,000–80,000 VND. Simple, authentic, and delicious.

day_by_day.notes: The Mausoleum has a strict dress code (no shorts, sleeveless tops). Photography is not allowed inside. Arrive before 9:00 AM to avoid queues. Book Water Puppet Show tickets in advance on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ninh Binh — catch a morning bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat bus station (~80,000–120,000 VND, ~2 hours). Upon arrival, rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000 VND/day) to explore the area. Visit Hoa Lu Ancient Capital — the 10th-century imperial citadel with ancient temples (~30,000 VND entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Row boat through Tam Coc ('Halong Bay on land') — ~150,000 VND for a 2-hour boat ride through stunning limestone karsts and rice paddies. The local rowers navigate through three natural caves. Optionally, climb 500 steps to Hang Mua viewpoint (~100,000 VND) for a panoramic vista.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by bus in the late afternoon/early evening. Rest and freshen up at the hotel. Enjoy a quiet evening exploring the Old Quarter's side streets and local eateries.

meals.breakfast: Grab a banh mi or xoi (sticky rice) from a street cart before catching the bus — ~20,000–35,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Local com binh dan (rice plate) restaurant near Tam Coc — rice with pork, vegetables, and soup for ~50,000–70,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Quan An Ngon on Phan Boi Chau Street — a popular open-air restaurant with many Vietnamese dishes, ~80,000–150,000 VND per person.

day_by_day.notes: Ninh Binh is a great budget day trip (~300,000–400,000 VND total including transport, entry, and boat). Start early to make the most of daylight. Bring sunscreen and a hat as the boat ride offers little shade.

day_by_day.morning: Take an overnight or early morning sleeper bus/train to Hue (~200,000–350,000 VND for a sleeper bus, ~14 hours — book via Sinh Tourist or The Sinh Tourist). If taking a day train, enjoy the scenic coastal route. Alternatively, book a budget flight (~500,000–800,000 VND on VietJet) to save time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hue. Check in to a budget hostel in the city center (~100,000–150,000 VND/night). Rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) and explore the Imperial Citadel of Hue (entry ~200,000 VND) — a UNESCO World Heritage site and former seat of the Nguyen emperors.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Perfume River at sunset. Visit Dong Ba Market for local snacks and souvenirs. Explore the lively streets around Pham Ngu Lao in Hue for cheap eats and cold beer.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the bus/train or grab something at Hanoi before departure.
meals.lunch: Banh mi or snacks purchased at a roadside stop during the journey.
meals.dinner: Bun Bo Hue (spicy Hue beef noodle soup) at a local street stall near Dong Ba Market — ~40,000–60,000 VND. This dish originates from Hue and is a must-try.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Hanoi–Hue transport at least 1–2 days in advance, especially for sleeper buses. The sleeper bus is the most budget-friendly option. Hue's Imperial Citadel is large — allow 2–3 hours to explore properly.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a motorbike (~100,000–150,000 VND/day) or join a cheap group tour (~150,000–200,000 VND) to explore Hue's Royal Tombs. Visit the Tomb of Tu Duc (entry ~100,000 VND) — the most elaborate and scenic of the tombs — set amid pine forests and lotus ponds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Thien Mu Pagoda (free entry) — Hue's iconic 7-story pagoda overlooking the Perfume River, a symbol of the city. Then explore the Tomb of Khai Dinh (~100,000 VND) — a striking blend of Vietnamese and European architectural styles built into a hillside.
day_by_day.evening: Take a sunset dragon boat cruise on the Perfume River (~100,000–150,000 VND per person) — a romantic and affordable Hue experience. Return to the city for dinner in the backpacker area.

meals.breakfast: Banh beo (steamed rice cakes with shrimp) from a local street vendor — ~30,000–50,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Com Hen (rice with baby clams) — a Hue specialty available at local markets for ~40,000–60,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Banh Khoai (Hue-style crispy pancake with shrimp and pork) at a local restaurant — ~60,000–80,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: A combo ticket for multiple royal tombs (~360,000 VND) can save money if visiting several. Motorbike rental requires an international driving permit or local license — check requirements. The dragon boat cruise can be arranged at the riverbank — negotiate the price.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus or grab a seat in a shared minivan to Hoi An (~100,000–150,000 VND, ~3–4 hours via the stunning Hai Van Pass coastal road). Alternatively, hire a motorbike driver for the scenic Hai Van Pass route (~200,000–300,000 VND) — one of Vietnam's most breathtaking coastal drives.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hoi An. Check in to a budget hostel in or near the Ancient Town (~100,000–150,000 VND/night). Explore the UNESCO-listed Hoi An Ancient Town on foot — visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge (entry included in Ancient Town ticket ~120,000 VND for 5 sites), old merchant houses, and colorful lantern-lined streets.
day_by_day.evening: Hoi An is famous for its magical lantern-lit evenings. Walk along the Thu Bon River at dusk and watch hundreds of silk lanterns glow. Release a flower lantern on the river (~20,000 VND) for good luck. Browse the night market for handmade souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure or grab a banh mi on the road.
meals.lunch: Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature noodle dish with pork and greens) at Trung Bac restaurant — ~60,000–80,000 VND.
meals.dinner: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Vac) at a riverside restaurant — ~60,000 VND. A Hoi An specialty not to be missed.

day_by_day.notes: The Ancient Town ticket gives access to 5 heritage sites — choose wisely based on your interests. Many streets in the Ancient Town are pedestrian-only in the evenings. Hoi An is very walkable — no need for transport within the old town.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–70,000 VND/day) and cycle to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach (~5 km from the Ancient Town) for a relaxing morning by the sea. The ride through rice paddies and villages is scenic and peaceful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town and join a budget cooking class (~200,000–350,000 VND) — Hoi An is one of Vietnam's best places to learn Vietnamese cooking. Classes typically include a market tour, hands-on cooking, and eating your creations. Alternatively, visit the Hoi An Museum of History and Culture (~30,000 VND) or browse the tailors on Le Loi Street.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Ancient Town one more time as the lanterns come alive at dusk. Visit the colorful Hoi An Central Market for local produce and street snacks. Enjoy a final Hoi An evening with a cold Huda beer (local Hue/Hoi An brand) at a riverside café.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong on Phan Chau Trinh Street — famous as the 'world's best banh mi' (featured by Anthony Bourdain) for ~35,000–45,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Mi Quang (turmeric noodles with pork, shrimp, and herbs) at a local eatery — ~50,000–70,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood at the Hoi An Night Market — grilled prawns, squid, and clams for ~100,000–150,000 VND total.

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance — popular ones fill up quickly. An Bang Beach has some beach bars but is generally quieter and less commercialized than Cua Dai. Carry cash as many small vendors don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus or sleeper bus south to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) — ~12–16 hours by bus (~250,000–400,000 VND) or book a budget flight (~600,000–1,000,000 VND on VietJet/Bamboo Airways, ~1 hour). If flying, depart from Da Nang Airport (~30 km from Hoi An, ~150,000 VND by taxi/grab).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ho Chi Minh City. Check in to a budget hostel in the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker district (~100,000–180,000 VND/night). Freshen up and head out to explore District 1. Visit the Reunification Palace (entry ~40,000 VND) — the former South Vietnamese presidential palace, frozen in time since 1975.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Ben Thanh Market — HCMC's iconic central market. Browse the indoor stalls for souvenirs, clothing, and local products. As the market closes at 6 PM, the surrounding streets transform into a lively outdoor night market with food stalls and bargain shopping.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure or grab food at the bus station/airport.
meals.lunch: Snacks on the bus or at a roadside stop, or airport food if flying.
meals.dinner: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork) at a street stall near Pham Ngu Lao — a HCMC staple for ~50,000–70,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: Book Hoi An–HCMC transport at least 1–2 days ahead. Flying is faster and often not much more expensive than the sleeper bus when booked in advance. HCMC traffic can be intense — use Grab (ride-hailing app) for affordable, hassle-free transport within the city.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Remnants Museum (entry ~40,000 VND) — one of Vietnam's most visited and emotionally powerful museums, documenting the Vietnam War through photographs and artifacts. Then walk to Notre Dame Cathedral and the historic Central Post Office (free to enter) — beautiful French colonial architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a Grab or local bus to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~40 km from HCMC) — entry ~110,000 VND, transport ~100,000–150,000 VND return. Explore the remarkable 250 km underground tunnel network used by Viet Cong soldiers during the war. Crawl through the tunnels and see wartime exhibits. Return to HCMC by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Vietnam — celebrate on Bui Vien Walking Street (HCMC's famous backpacker street) with cheap cocktails, live music, and street food. Soak in the electric atmosphere. Do last-minute souvenir shopping at the nearby markets.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi from a street cart near the hostel — ~25,000–40,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Snacks at Cu Chi Tunnels or a local com binh dan restaurant near the site — ~50,000–70,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Pho 2000 or a local pho restaurant near Pham Ngu Lao for a nostalgic final bowl of pho — ~60,000–80,000 VND. End with a Vietnamese iced coffee (ca phe sua da) at a sidewalk café.

day_by_day.notes: Cu Chi Tunnels can be visited independently or via a cheap group tour (~150,000–200,000 VND including transport). Book early morning to avoid the midday heat. The War Remnants Museum is sobering — allow 1.5–2 hours. Keep some VND for last-minute purchases and tips. Total estimated daily budget: 400,000–700,000 VND (~$16–$28 USD) per day excluding accommodation and long-distance transport.

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hanoi Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to boutique hotel in the Old Quarter (approximately 45 minutes by taxi or Grab app, ~200,000 VND). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle stroll through the iconic 36 Streets of the Old Quarter. Explore Hang Gai (Silk Street), Hang Bac (Silver Street), and soak in the chaotic charm of Hanoi's oldest neighborhood. Visit Ngoc Son Temple on Hoan Kiem Lake (entrance ~30,000 VND) for a peaceful introduction to Vietnamese culture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ta Hien Street — known as 'Beer Corner' — for a lively first evening. Grab a plastic stool, order a Bia Hoi (fresh draft beer, ~5,000–10,000 VND per glass) and watch the city buzz around you. Wander the illuminated Old Quarter streets before turning in early to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Bun Cha Huong Lien (near Old Quarter) — famous bun cha (grilled pork with noodles), ~60,000–80,000 VND. The spot made famous by Anthony Bourdain and Barack Obama.
meals.dinner: Pho Thin Bo Ho — a legendary pho restaurant on Dinh Tien Hoang Street. A steaming bowl of beef pho for ~60,000–80,000 VND. Simple, authentic, and perfect for night one.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light to allow recovery from the flight. Use the evening to download the Grab app for easy and affordable transportation throughout Vietnam. Exchange currency at a bank or ATM in the Old Quarter for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a traditional Vietnamese breakfast at a local street stall, then visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex (open mornings only, closed Mondays and Fridays). See the Presidential Palace, Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House, and the One Pillar Pagoda. Entrance to the complex is free but the mausoleum itself requires modest dress and respectful conduct.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND entrance) — one of Southeast Asia's best ethnographic museums, showcasing Vietnam's 54 ethnic minority groups through artifacts, clothing, and reconstructed village homes. Take a Grab to reach it (~30,000–40,000 VND from Old Quarter).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter for a Vietnamese cooking class or street food walking tour (~300,000–500,000 VND). Learn about local ingredients, taste multiple dishes, and connect with fellow travelers. Finish the night with a ca phe trung (egg coffee) at Cafe Giang, a Hanoi institution.

meals.breakfast: Xoi Yen on Nguyen Huu Huan Street — sticky rice with various toppings like mung bean, chicken, or fried shallots. ~25,000–40,000 VND. A true Hanoian breakfast staple.
meals.lunch: Banh Mi 25 on Hang Ca Street — widely regarded as one of Hanoi's best banh mi spots. Crispy baguette with pate, cold cuts, pickled vegetables. ~35,000–50,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong on Cha Ca Street — the restaurant so famous it gave the street its name. Turmeric-marinated fish grilled tableside with dill and scallions. ~150,000–200,000 VND per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays, Fridays, and for several weeks in October–November for maintenance. Confirm opening hours before visiting. Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees) for the mausoleum and pagodas.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ninh Binh (approximately 2 hours south of Hanoi by bus or booked minivan, ~100,000–150,000 VND). Arrive and head straight to Trang An Landscape Complex — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Take a 2.5-hour rowing boat tour through stunning limestone karsts, grottos, and ancient temples (~250,000 VND per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000 VND/day) and cycle to Bich Dong Pagoda, a beautiful three-level pagoda built into a limestone cliff. Then pedal to the ancient capital of Hoa Lu to explore the 10th-century royal temples of Dinh Tien Hoang and Le Dai Hanh.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by bus or minivan in the late afternoon. Arrive back in the Old Quarter by early evening. Relax at a rooftop bar on Luong Van Can Street with views over the Old Quarter before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Com Pho 49 near the hotel — simple Vietnamese rice porridge (chao) or pho to fuel up before the day trip. ~40,000–60,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Trang An — try com nieu (clay pot rice) or bun cha Ninh Binh with goat meat (de nuong), a regional specialty. ~80,000–120,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Bia Hoi Junction (Ta Hien / Luong Ngoc Quyen corner) — grilled skewers, nem ran (fried spring rolls), and cold beer in the open air. ~80,000–150,000 VND total.

day_by_day.notes: Book a Ninh Binh day trip through your hotel or a reputable local agency the night before. The Trang An boat tour can get busy — aim to arrive early (by 8:30–9:00 AM). Bring sunscreen and a hat as the boat ride is largely exposed.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Ha Long Bay. Take a booked overnight cruise departing from Hanoi (~3.5-hour drive to the pier). Mid-range 2-day/1-night cruises on Ha Long Bay cost approximately $80–$130 USD per person and include meals, kayaking, and cave visits. Embark around noon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cruise through the emerald waters of Ha Long Bay, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visit Sung Sot Cave (Surprise Cave) — one of the largest and most impressive grottos in the bay. Kayak through hidden lagoons and floating fishing villages.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset from the cruise deck with drinks in hand. Participate in a cooking demonstration on board. Dinner is served as part of the cruise package with fresh seafood. Sleep in a comfortable cabin on the water.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast near the Old Quarter before departure — banh cuon (steamed rice rolls) with pork and mushrooms at a street stall. ~30,000–50,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Included as part of the cruise package — typically a multi-course Vietnamese seafood lunch served on board.
meals.dinner: Included in the cruise package — fresh grilled seafood, spring rolls, stir-fried vegetables, and Vietnamese soup served in the cruise dining room.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Ha Long Bay cruise at least 2–3 days in advance. Choose a reputable mid-range operator such as Indochina Junk, Paradise Cruises (budget tier), or Bhaya Cruises. Avoid the cheapest budget boats for safety and experience quality. Pack a small overnight bag as large luggage is often left at the pier storage.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for sunrise over Ha Long Bay from the cruise deck — a truly magical experience. Morning tai chi session offered on the top deck. Enjoy a final kayaking session or visit a pearl farm before breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cruise returns to the pier by midday. Transfer back to Hanoi (3.5 hours). Take an overnight sleeper train or bus from Hanoi to Hue (departs around 19:00–21:00, approximately 13–14 hours, ~250,000–400,000 VND for a soft sleeper berth).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Hanoi train station. Grab dinner near the station before boarding. The overnight train to Hue is a classic backpacker experience — comfortable soft-sleeper cabins with 4 or 6 berths.

meals.breakfast: Included in the cruise package — eggs, toast, fresh fruit, Vietnamese coffee served on board.
meals.lunch: Included in the cruise package — final lunch served before disembarking, typically Vietnamese staples with seafood.
meals.dinner: Bun Bo Nam Bo near Hanoi train station (Ga Ha Noi) — dry beef noodle salad with herbs and fried shallots. ~60,000–80,000 VND. Quick, satisfying pre-train meal.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Hanoi–Hue overnight train (SE trains are recommended) in advance via the Vietnam Railways website or a local travel agent. Bring a travel pillow, earplugs, and a light jacket as the air conditioning can be cold. Secure your valuables in your bag while sleeping.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive in Hue early morning (around 07:00–09:00). Check into a guesthouse or boutique hotel near the Citadel (~300,000–500,000 VND/night). Freshen up, then head straight to the Imperial Citadel of Hue — the former seat of the Nguyen Dynasty. Explore the Forbidden Purple City, the Thai Hoa Palace, and the beautiful gates and moats. (~150,000 VND entrance).
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or hire a xe om (motorbike taxi) to visit the Royal Tombs along the Perfume River. The Tomb of Khai Dinh (~150,000 VND) is the most visually stunning — a dramatic fusion of Vietnamese and European architecture. Also visit the Tomb of Minh Mang for its serene garden setting.
day_by_day.evening: Walk across the iconic Truong Tien Bridge at sunset for panoramic views of the Perfume River. Explore the vibrant Dong Ba Market for local crafts, conical hats, and street snacks. Enjoy a leisurely riverside dinner.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong (or a local equivalent in Hue) — or better yet, try bun bo Hue (spicy beef noodle soup), Hue's most famous dish, at a local street stall near the market. ~40,000–60,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Com Hen on Hen Island — tiny clam rice with crispy pork skin, peanuts, and herbs. A quintessential Hue dish sold by street vendors. ~25,000–40,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Lac Thien Restaurant on Dinh Tien Hoang Street — a beloved local institution run by a deaf family. Try banh khoai (Hue sizzling crepes), nem lui (lemongrass pork skewers), and banh beo (steamed rice cakes). ~100,000–150,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: Hue's cuisine is considered the most refined and complex in Vietnam — take time to explore the local food scene. The Imperial Citadel is large; wear comfortable shoes. April weather in Hue can be warm and humid — stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Hue to Hoi An via the Hai Van Pass — one of Vietnam's most scenic routes. Take a booked minivan or join a group tour that stops at the pass for photos (~150,000–200,000 VND). The journey takes approximately 3–4 hours with stops. Arrive in Hoi An by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a guesthouse in or near Hoi An Ancient Town (~300,000–500,000 VND/night). Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town on foot: visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge, Phung Hung Old House, Tan Ky Merchant House, and browse the tailors and lantern shops along Tran Phu Street. Purchase a combined ticket (~120,000 VND) for access to heritage sites.
day_by_day.evening: Join the magical lantern-lit streets of Hoi An as night falls — the Ancient Town transforms into a glowing wonderland. Release a lantern on the Thu Bon River (~20,000–30,000 VND) for good luck. Explore the night market on Nguyen Hoang Street.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast in Hue before departure — banh mi or a bowl of chao (rice porridge) from a street vendor near the guesthouse. ~20,000–40,000 VND.
meals.lunch: White Rose Restaurant in Hoi An — the only place in the world serving authentic Hoi An white rose dumplings (banh bao vac) and cao lau noodles. ~80,000–150,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Banh Mi Phuong on Phan Chau Trinh Street — Anthony Bourdain called it 'the world's best banh mi.' ~35,000–50,000 VND. Follow with fresh fruit juice from a street cart.

day_by_day.notes: The Hai Van Pass is best enjoyed on a clear day — check weather conditions. If you're comfortable on a motorbike, renting one (~120,000–150,000 VND/day) to ride the pass yourself is an unforgettable experience. Hoi An Ancient Town is pedestrian-only in the evenings — park bicycles outside the core area.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000 VND/day) and cycle 4 km to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach for a relaxed morning by the South China Sea. Swim, sunbathe, or simply enjoy the coastal scenery. An Bang is slightly less crowded and more backpacker-friendly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hoi An and take a half-day cooking class (~400,000–600,000 VND) — many excellent options are available in the Ancient Town. Visit the local market with a chef guide, learn to make cao lau, fresh spring rolls, and a Vietnamese dessert. This is one of the best cultural activities in Vietnam.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the tailors and artisan workshops of Hoi An — the town is famous for custom-made clothing at affordable prices (budget 1–2 days for tailoring if ordering). Browse the lantern-lit streets once more, pick up handmade souvenirs, and enjoy a final evening in this enchanting town.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong again (it's that good) or try Mi Quang 1A on Truong Minh Luong — turmeric noodles with shrimp, pork, and herbs. A Hoi An breakfast classic. ~40,000–60,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Included in the cooking class — you eat what you cook! A full Vietnamese meal prepared by your own hands.
meals.dinner: Morning Glory Restaurant on Tran Phu Street — upscale street food in a beautiful setting. Try their cao lau, white rose dumplings, and crispy wonton. ~150,000–250,000 VND per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class the day before to secure a spot. Hoi An's beaches can be affected by jellyfish seasonally — ask locals before swimming. If ordering custom clothing from a tailor, do so on Day 7 evening to allow time for fittings and pickup.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon). Take a taxi or Grab from Hoi An to Da Nang Airport (~200,000–250,000 VND, 30 minutes). Domestic flights run frequently (~500,000–900,000 VND on VietJet or Bamboo Airways). Arrive in Ho Chi Minh City by midday. Check into a guesthouse or boutique hotel in District 1 or the Backpacker District (Pham Ngu Lao area, ~300,000–600,000 VND/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into Saigon's history at the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) — a powerful and sobering account of the Vietnam War from the Vietnamese perspective. Then visit the Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND), the former South Vietnamese presidential palace frozen in time since 1975.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Bui Vien Walking Street — Saigon's famous backpacker strip — for a lively, chaotic, neon-lit evening. Street food stalls, live music, and cold beer create an electric atmosphere. A quintessential Southeast Asia backpacker experience.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a café near your Hoi An guesthouse before the airport transfer — banh mi or pho. ~30,000–50,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Pho Quynh on Pham Ngu Lao Street — a Saigon institution for beef pho. Open 24 hours, beloved by locals and travelers alike. ~60,000–80,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Banh Xeo 46A on Dinh Cong Trang Street — famous sizzling Vietnamese crepes (banh xeo) stuffed with shrimp, pork, and bean sprouts, wrapped in rice paper with fresh herbs. ~80,000–120,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Da Nang–Ho Chi Minh City flight at least 3–4 days in advance for the best prices. Ho Chi Minh City traffic is notoriously chaotic — use Grab for all transportation. The War Remnants Museum is emotionally intense; allow time to process the exhibits.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~70 km northwest of Saigon, ~1.5 hours by booked tour or Grab). Explore the 250 km network of underground tunnels used by Viet Cong guerrillas during the war. Crawl through narrow tunnel sections, see booby traps, and gain a visceral understanding of wartime ingenuity. (~110,000 VND entrance, tours from ~200,000–300,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Saigon by early afternoon. Visit Ben Thanh Market for last-minute souvenir shopping — lacquerware, silk scarves, coffee, and dried fruits. Bargain confidently. Then walk to the nearby Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica and the ornate Saigon Central Post Office (both free to visit) for a taste of French colonial architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Vietnam — celebrate the journey with a rooftop dinner or cocktails at a sky bar in District 1 (Chill Skybar or Broma Not a Bar offer stunning city views at mid-range prices). Reflect on 10 incredible days. Head to Tan Son Nhat Airport for your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Hu Tieu Nam Vang near Pham Ngu Lao — Cambodian-style clear noodle soup with pork, shrimp, and quail eggs. A beloved Saigon breakfast. ~50,000–70,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Com Tam Thuan Kieu near Ben Thanh Market — broken rice (com tam) with grilled pork chop, shredded pork skin, fried egg, and pickled vegetables. The quintessential Saigon lunch. ~60,000–90,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Nha Hang Ngon on Nam Ky Khoi Nghia Street — a beautiful colonial villa courtyard restaurant serving dishes from all regions of Vietnam. A perfect final meal to recap the flavors of your journey. ~150,000–250,000 VND per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Cu Chi Tunnels tour the evening before. The Ben Ben tunnels section (further from Saigon) is less touristy and more authentic than the closer Dia Chi Cu area — worth requesting if booking a private tour. Allow at least 3 hours at the airport before international departure. Keep some cash for airport snacks and any last-minute expenses.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Take a pre-arranged private luxury transfer to your boutique hotel in the Old Quarter. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation stroll through the narrow lanes of the 36 Streets of the Old Quarter – explore Hang Gai (Silk Street), Hang Bac (Silver Street), and soak in the colonial French architecture and vibrant street life.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a welcome cocktail at the hotel rooftop bar overlooking the Old Quarter skyline. Head to Hoan Kiem Lake for the evening promenade and visit the illuminated Ngoc Son Temple on Jade Island. End the night with a premium street food walking tour of the Old Quarter sampling Banh Mi, Pho, and Bun Cha from curated top-tier street vendors.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Light welcome snack platter at the hotel upon check-in
meals.dinner: Guided premium street food tour dinner in the Old Quarter – highlights include Pho Thin (iconic beef pho), Bun Cha Huong Lien, and fresh Banh Cuon from a heritage vendor

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer with your hotel concierge in advance. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. The Old Quarter is walkable from the hotel – wear comfortable shoes for the evening stroll.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a traditional Vietnamese breakfast at the hotel or a nearby renowned local spot. Join a private morning cyclo tour through the Old Quarter's 36 guild streets with a knowledgeable local guide. Visit Dong Xuan Market – Hanoi's oldest and largest covered market – for a cultural immersion into local trade, spices, and textiles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) – Vietnam's first national university dating to 1070 – with a private guide explaining its Confucian heritage. Continue to the Fine Arts Museum of Vietnam for a curated tour of Vietnamese lacquerware, silk paintings, and revolutionary art. Stop at a premium silk boutique on Hang Gai Street for bespoke souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Water Puppet Show at the Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre – a UNESCO-recognized art form unique to northern Vietnam. Follow with a refined dinner at a top-tier Hanoi restaurant specializing in elevated northern Vietnamese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Op La (Vietnamese egg baguette) and Ca Phe Trung (egg coffee) at Cafe Giang – a Hanoi institution since 1946
meals.lunch: Bun Cha at Bun Cha Dac Kim – a legendary Old Quarter restaurant famed for its grilled pork and rice noodles
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cha Ca Thang Long – renowned for its signature Cha Ca La Vong (turmeric grilled fish with dill), a Hanoi culinary icon

day_by_day.notes: Book the Water Puppet Show in advance as performances fill up quickly. The Temple of Literature is best visited in the morning to avoid afternoon heat and crowds.

day_by_day.date: Day 3 – April 17, 2027 (Hanoi Heritage & Ho Chi Minh Quarter)
day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex (open mornings only, closed Mondays and Fridays) – see the Presidential Palace, Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House, and the One Pillar Pagoda. Explore the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology for an in-depth understanding of Vietnam's 54 ethnic minority groups through world-class exhibits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Hoa Lo Prison Museum (the 'Hanoi Hilton') for a sobering and historically rich experience. Walk through the French Quarter to admire the grand colonial architecture – St. Joseph's Cathedral, the Opera House, and the historic Metropole Hotel. Arrange a private behind-the-scenes tour of the Metropole's wartime bunker.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sunset cocktails at the Sofitel Legend Metropole's Le Club Bar – a Hanoi institution. Explore the vibrant Ta Hien Street (Beer Corner) for a curated craft beer and local snack experience, then dine at a premium restaurant for a multi-course Vietnamese tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Full Vietnamese breakfast buffet at the hotel
meals.lunch: Pho Bo (beef pho) at Pho Bat Dan – one of Hanoi's most celebrated and authentic pho establishments
meals.dinner: Tasting menu dinner at La Badiane – a celebrated French-Vietnamese fusion fine dining restaurant in the French Quarter

day_by_day.notes: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum has a strict dress code – cover shoulders and knees. Arrive early (before 9:00 AM) to avoid long queues. Photography is restricted inside the mausoleum.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hanoi at 07:30 by private luxury vehicle for Ninh Binh (approximately 2 hours). Upon arrival, board a traditional rowing boat for a scenic cruise through Trang An Landscape Complex – a UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring dramatic limestone karsts, hidden caves, and ancient temples reflected in emerald waterways.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike to the summit of Mua Cave (Hang Mua) for panoramic views over the Tam Coc rice paddies and karst mountains – one of Vietnam's most iconic vistas. Visit the ancient capital of Hoa Lu and its 10th-century royal temples dedicated to the Dinh and Le dynasties.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by private vehicle (arriving approximately 19:30). Freshen up at the hotel and enjoy a relaxed evening dinner in the Old Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a premium riverside restaurant in Ninh Binh – featuring local specialties including Com Chay (crispy rice), goat meat, and freshwater fish
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nha Hang Ngon – a beautifully restored colonial villa restaurant serving authentic Vietnamese regional dishes in an elegant garden setting

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes for the Mua Cave climb (approximately 500 steps). Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water. Book the private vehicle and boat tour in advance through your hotel concierge.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 – April 19, 2027 (Travel to Ha Long Bay)
day_by_day.morning: Check out of the Old Quarter hotel. Private luxury transfer departs at 08:00 for Ha Long Bay (approximately 3.5 hours). En route, stop at a premium lacquerware and ceramics workshop in Bat Trang Ceramic Village for a hands-on cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board your luxury overnight cruise vessel at Ha Long Bay's International Cruise Port. Settle into your private cabin, enjoy a welcome lunch on deck as the boat sails into the bay. Kayak through hidden lagoons and explore the stunning limestone karst formations of Ha Long Bay – a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the sundeck with panoramic views of the bay. Enjoy a premium seafood cooking class on board, followed by a multi-course gourmet dinner featuring freshly caught seafood. Squid fishing from the deck under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before check-out
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch on board the cruise – fresh spring rolls, grilled seafood, and Vietnamese salads
meals.dinner: Gourmet multi-course dinner on the cruise – lobster, tiger prawns, steamed fish with ginger, and Vietnamese desserts

day_by_day.notes: Select a premium 5-star cruise line such as Indochine Cruise, Paradise Elegance, or Orchid Classic for the best luxury experience. Pack light for the overnight cruise – leave large luggage stored at a hotel or with your transfer service.

day_by_day.date: Day 6 – April 20, 2027 (Ha Long Bay Exploration & Travel to Hoi An)
day_by_day.morning: Early morning Tai Chi session on the sundeck at sunrise. Explore Sung Sot (Surprise) Cave – Ha Long Bay's largest and most spectacular grotto. Visit a floating fishing village for an authentic glimpse into the lives of Ha Long's water-dwelling communities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to port by noon. Private luxury transfer to Noi Bai Airport for an afternoon domestic flight to Da Nang (approximately 1.5 hours). Upon arrival in Da Nang, private transfer to Hoi An (approximately 45 minutes). Check into your luxury boutique hotel in Hoi An Ancient Town.
day_by_day.evening: First evening in Hoi An – stroll through the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town as the lanterns illuminate the Thu Bon River. Visit the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge and explore the beautifully preserved merchant houses. Enjoy a riverside dinner at a premium Hoi An restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast on board the cruise before disembarkation
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the cruise port or during transfer
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Cargo Club Restaurant in Hoi An – a celebrated riverside fine dining venue renowned for its Vietnamese and international cuisine and spectacular river views

day_by_day.notes: Confirm domestic flight booking well in advance. Hoi An Ancient Town is best explored on foot – the hotel should be within walking distance of the main sights. The Ancient Town charges a modest entrance fee via ticket booklets.

day_by_day.morning: Join a premium private cooking class starting with a guided tour of Hoi An's Central Market to select fresh local ingredients. Learn to prepare signature Hoi An dishes including White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac), Cao Lau noodles, and Banh Mi Phuong under the guidance of a master chef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ancient Town with a private cultural guide – visit the Tan Ky Ancient House (200-year-old merchant home), the Phuc Kien Assembly Hall (Fujian Chinese community temple), and the Museum of Trading Ceramics. Commission a custom tailored outfit at one of Hoi An's renowned bespoke tailor shops on Le Loi Street.
day_by_day.evening: Boat ride along the Thu Bon River at sunset, releasing lanterns onto the water – a deeply atmospheric Hoi An tradition. Explore the vibrant Night Market on An Hoi Island for artisan crafts and street food. Dinner at a premium restaurant specializing in Central Vietnamese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi from Banh Mi Phuong – arguably Vietnam's most famous banh mi shop, a Hoi An institution
meals.lunch: Lunch prepared during your cooking class – enjoy the dishes you created
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mango Mango Restaurant – a sophisticated open-air venue on the riverfront serving elevated Vietnamese and fusion cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class and tailor appointments in advance. Allow 24-48 hours for tailored clothing to be completed. The lantern release boat ride is best arranged through your hotel concierge for a private experience.

day_by_day.date: Day 8 – April 22, 2027 (My Son Sanctuary & Beach Relaxation)
day_by_day.morning: Early private guided excursion to My Son Sanctuary – a UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring ancient Cham Hindu temple ruins dating from the 4th to 14th centuries, set dramatically within a jungle valley. A private guide will provide deep historical and archaeological context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hoi An and transfer to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach for a premium afternoon beach experience. Relax at a top-tier beach club with sun loungers, fresh coconuts, and ocean views. Optional: paddleboarding, snorkeling, or a beachside spa treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beachfront bar. Return to Hoi An Ancient Town for a final evening of exploration – browse artisan galleries, silk shops, and lantern boutiques. Enjoy a farewell Hoi An dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a premium beachfront restaurant at An Bang Beach – grilled prawns, clams, and local fish
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hai Scout Cafe or Streets Restaurant Hoi An – the latter is a social enterprise restaurant training disadvantaged youth in hospitality, offering exceptional Vietnamese cuisine

day_by_day.notes: My Son is best visited early morning before the heat intensifies. Wear light, breathable clothing and bring insect repellent for the jungle site. The beach clubs at An Bang Beach offer premium day-use facilities.

day_by_day.date: Day 9 – April 23, 2027 (Travel to Ho Chi Minh City)
day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Hoi An – enjoy a slow breakfast and last-minute shopping in the Ancient Town. Check out and transfer to Da Nang Airport for a morning domestic flight to Ho Chi Minh City (approximately 1.5 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon). Private luxury transfer to your premium hotel in District 1. After check-in, explore the historic core of Saigon – visit Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica, the Central Post Office (designed by Gustave Eiffel), and the Reunification Palace with a private guided tour.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Saigon's legendary street food scene on a premium guided motorbike food tour through the city's best neighborhoods – sampling Banh Xeo (sizzling crepes), Com Tam (broken rice), and fresh Goi Cuon (spring rolls) from iconic local spots. End with rooftop cocktails at a sky bar overlooking the city skyline.

meals.breakfast: Final Hoi An breakfast at the hotel – Cao Lau noodles and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Da Nang Airport or upon arrival in Ho Chi Minh City
meals.dinner: Premium motorbike street food tour dinner covering 5-6 iconic Saigon street food stops across Districts 1, 3, and 4

day_by_day.notes: Book the motorbike food tour with a reputable operator such as Saigon Street Eats or XO Tours for a premium, safe experience. The Reunification Palace requires advance booking for guided tours. Keep valuables secure in Ho Chi Minh City.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Remnants Museum for a powerful and comprehensive account of the Vietnam War – one of the most significant museums in Southeast Asia. Explore the Ben Thanh Market area for final souvenir shopping – premium lacquerware, silk, coffee, and local spices. Visit a specialty Vietnamese coffee roaster for a curated coffee tasting experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional half-day excursion to the Cu Chi Tunnels (approximately 1.5 hours from the city) – explore the extraordinary 250km underground tunnel network used by Viet Cong forces during the war, with a private expert guide. Alternatively, enjoy a premium spa afternoon at your hotel or a luxury day spa in District 1 for final relaxation before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Ho Chi Minh City's finest restaurants. Final evening stroll along Nguyen Hue Walking Street and Dong Khoi Street. Private luxury transfer to Tan Son Nhat International Airport for departure.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork) at Com Tam Ba Ghien – a beloved Saigon institution, or a premium lunch at a District 1 restaurant
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Noir Dining in the Dark or Cuc Gach Quan – a beautifully restored heritage villa restaurant serving refined home-style Vietnamese cuisine beloved by locals and discerning travelers alike

day_by_day.notes: The Cu Chi Tunnels excursion requires approximately 4-5 hours including travel – only recommended if departing late evening. Confirm airport transfer timing with your hotel concierge based on your flight schedule. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security.
